entries.quote: It chose a fantastic art direction by making them chibi and cute.
entries.why: Argon's chibi characters, as a direction. Ken hasn't named a specific piece as the best example yet.
Koto as a woodblock print and as an ink painting. Ken liked all three directions in the study; the third, hariko, has since been rejected.
Argon low-poly station, seen enlarged in light and dark. The model for the other Town buildings once it is checked at real size. On branch art/town-station-lowpoly.

entries.quote: I like Musashi's complexity. His hair is in-depth and textured, his outfit stylized with many attributes, it's awesome.
entries.why: The level of designed detail Ken wants on a character: textured hair and a stylized outfit with many attributes.

entries.quote: I think the polymetric designs from Kingdoms and castles are good. The highlight of it is its simplicity yet complexity in design.
entries.why: The look chosen for the Town: faceted, isometric low-poly shapes drawn in 2D. The server concept sheet is a direction, not art to ship.

entries.quote: I like the light mode palette and how it blends.
entries.why: The light theme colors. Keep them; dark mode wasn't mentioned.

entries.quote: I like the combat style direction.
entries.why: The direction of the battle screens.

entries.quote: I like the art of the monster sprites.
entries.why: The foe art, with limits. Ken later called them "the best designed", but said details "like the eyes being too simplistic and the animations being a bit wonky hold it back". Not a reference to copy; only a starting point to "add complexity to the current design".

entries.quote: Nine Sols, kingdoms and castles, Lil guardsman, ori and the will of the wisps, night in the woods for art.
entries.why: Games whose look Ken loves, summed up as "the type of chibi and kind of simplistic style I'm looking for." They guide the replacement for hariko; learn from them, and never copy their characters or art.

entries.quote: I hate the toy aesthetic completely. The red and white and blue designs are fugly.
entries.why: All hariko and painted toy art, in the game and in tests. Asked if that included the game's plan, Ken said "Yes. I hate all of it."

entries.quote: It looks like any regular plain old Home Screen. I dislike it because of how simple it is, it's the first thing our users see. It should be stylized. Creative. It should take risks.
entries.why: A safe, tidied-up Home. Ken loved the content, disliked the format, and asked for a redesign rather than an edit.
Argon's two Home concepts: the scene as the UI, and the emaki scroll. The reasons weren't recorded.

entries.quote: the animations GPT made are much too flashy, I just need a thin white slice effect and damage effect and hurt anim and KO anim and special KO effect.
entries.why: Busy battle effects. Ken wants restraint: a thin slice and clear reactions.

entries.quote: The bushes look a bit rough visually. Like sloppy circles. Same for the walking animation at the beginning, he just bounces.
entries.why: Blobby shapes built from circles, and walking that's only a bounce.
